registered_before: the diurnal normal capture starts; no data under the diurnal profile exists
owner_decisions: 21/11: try a protocol whose load covers every regime, not most learning and live data in one regime
21/11: the load must follow the real regimes over at least 24 h (peak around 08:00, few requests 00:00-06:00, ...), designed to match real demand
problem: every capture and live run so far applied the five regimes only in the first 90 minutes (two cycles, 756 s then 324 s per regime) and then 'steady' to the end: about 88 % of a 12 h capture and almost all of a live run were one regime, so the models learnt steady traffic and the burden under other loads is unmeasured

profile.day_plan_local_time_utc+7: 00:00 night, 02:00 toolmix (maintenance 30 min), 02:30 night, 05:30 recovery, 07:00 steady, 08:00 peak, 08:30 burst (login storm 10 min), 08:40 peak, 10:00 toolmix, 11:30 peak (lunch), 13:00 steady, 14:30 toolmix (1 h), 15:30 steady, 19:00 peak, 20:00 burst (flash sale 15 min), 20:15 peak, 21:30 recovery, 23:00 night
profile.jitter: every boundary after 00:00 moves by a seeded uniform jitter of up to +/-10 min per calendar day (seed in CONFIG.json)
profile.hours_per_day: night 5.9, steady 6.5, peak 5.4, toolmix 2.9, recovery 2.7, burst 0.6
profile.night_regime: 1 east-west and 1 ingress loadgen replica, no read-mix, 1 dependency, sleep 4 s, ingress interval 1.0 s, frontend 1.2 s

steps.C_capture: pulse-token-capture-diurnal-<MMDD>: 24 h (SECONDS_TOTAL 86400) of normal traffic under the diurnal profile, lineage token build pulse-tokens-final-f8ccbb2, no campaign, K8s events recorded; no heavy job on any node while it runs
steps.A_aging: descriptive, after C: the deployed t3 models (pulse-live-v7-fit-1118, learnt on steady-heavy data) score the whole capture; held-out style exceedance of 60 s container blocks per regime (scripts/analysis/model_aging.py with the regime of each block from PHASES.jsonl)
steps.F_fit: t3 fit on the capture plus the final run's normal tail (pulse-live-final-1119 after its campaign; lineage, 9.5 h steady) with the registered parameters (top 3, trim 0.005, alpha' 0.0003, 5-fold cross-fit over 30 min chunks, 60 s blocks); held-out exceedance per regime reported
steps.L_live: pulse-live-diurnal-<MMDD>: the final run's campaign (pulse-live-final-v1 options) under the diurnal profile for the whole run, SECONDS_TOTAL at least the campaign plus 12 h of normal tail, so the tail spans night and day; the alert path is t3 alone unless session-stream-v1 adopts a session branch before L starts, in which case that system is the alert path and the comparison with t3 alone is done offline on the same windows

hypotheses.H0: primary set: recall >= 95 %, idle control <= 5 %, precision >= 95 %, p95 kernel -> end of alarm window <= 3 s (as pulse-live-final-v1)
hypotheses.H9: recall >= 95 % within every regime that holds at least 30 primary-set trials (trial regime = regime at the interval start)
hypotheses.H10: burden per regime on the normal tail: no regime above 3 times the pooled burden (a model that learnt every regime has no regime it does not know)

reported: A: exceedance per regime of the steady-trained models on diurnal data
F: held-out exceedance per regime of the diurnal fit
L: everything pulse-live-final-v1 reports, plus recall, control, admin, harmless-binary and burden per regime, and the same against the final run
trial counts per regime (the campaign runs through day and night)
limits: the profile is designed, not replayed from a real shop's logs; the regimes are the loadgen settings of the testbed
one diurnal capture of 24 h: each regime appears on one day of learning data, so day-to-day variation of the same regime is only the seeded jitter
rules: runs complete their full cycle; infrastructure faults are excluded spans, not a reason to stop
no heavy job on any node while C or L runs
any change to the model that scores LID-DS reruns LID-DS 2021 and keeps the t3 dataset result (improvements-must-rerun rule); the diurnal profile changes only cluster learning data
